## Most serious finding

`card-search.md`§1.2's `CheckCardProperties` gate: claimed the "show anime cards"/whitelist exception applies to all three of `TYPE_TOKEN`, `SCOPE_HIDDEN`, and non-official `ot`. It doesn't — `&&` binds tighter than `||` in the actual condition, so the exception is scoped to the non-official-`ot` clause only. Token and Hidden-scope cards are excluded **unconditionally** by upstream's own search; nothing reveals them. A future implementer reading only the doc would have built a visibility rule upstream doesn't have.

## Systematic cause (required investigation 5)

Two distinct, nameable classes, not seven unrelated slips:

1. **Line-range citations that stop one line short of a function's real closing brace.** Present in 5 of 7 documents, ~15 instances total, all in the same direction (undershoot, never counting the standalone `}` as part of the function). The two *overshoot* instances found in Round 1 (`deck-builder-legality.md`'s `push_side`, extending 4 lines past its own close into `pop_main`) are the outlier — same document, same trio of near-identical sibling functions, looks like scrolling past the right stopping point once and reusing the range. A future automated check is plausible here: given a cited "whole function" range and the function name, a brace-matching scan of the cited file could confirm the range's end line is exactly the closing `}` — this is the kind of check brief 003's framework-hardening work suggests this project is willing to build.
2. **Claiming a behavior is symmetric across a pair of functions/branches after verifying only one side.** Three separate instances, three separate documents: `deck-model.md`'s `LoadDeck` reclassification (main→extra is type-checked, extra→main is not), `card-search.md`'s `deck_sort_*` comparators (three of five are type-aware, two aren't, and the type-aware ones don't even order the same way as each other), `deck-builder-ui.md`'s `ShowCardInfo` attack/defense check (the Link branch never checks defense at all). Fewer instances than class 1, but higher-value: these are wrong behavioral claims, not stale numbers.
